recipes.name: Hungarian Goulash
ingredients_raw: 3 pounds beef stew meat, cut into 1 1/2 inch cubes

steps.text: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Cook and stir onions in oil until soft, 2 to 4 minutes. Remove onions and set them aside.
Combine paprika, 2 teaspoons salt, and pepper in a medium bowl. Coat beef cubes in spice mixture and cook in the onion pot until brown on all sides.

Return onions to the pot with beef; pour in water, tomato paste, garlic, and remaining 1 teaspoon salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, until meat is tender, 1 1/2 to 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Hungarian Goulash
raw_recipe.description: Try this Hungarian goulash recipe featuring slowly stewed beef chuck with onion, garlic, tomato paste, and sweet paprika for a mildly spicy comfort food dish.

video.description: In this video, you’ll see how to make Hungarian goulash. It's always a family favorite. Cubes of beef chuck are stewed until tender with sautéed onions, garlic, sweet Hungarian paprika, and tomato paste. Enjoy this rich stew spooned over egg noodles, rice, or mashed potatoes.

review.reviewBody:
Good basic recipe that can be adjusted to taste. Hungarian goulash should be a flexible recipe, and you should taste it and adjust it when it is almost cooked, to suit your own taste. I am of Hungarian origin and these changes come close to my grandma’s goulash: there is no need to separate the onions from the meat, stir fry the onion, then add the meat, stir fry again, the add all other ingredients to the same pot except the water, stir fry again, then add the water last. Feel free to vary this according to what you have at home. Tomato instead of tomato paste, Or even no tomato! 
 I add 2-3 tbsp more paprika (the sweet kind, not the hot kind) half as much tomato paste, and may add some chopped green pepper (no more than 1/2 cup), a bit more garlic, I always add 2-3 tbsp soy sauce, and even a bit of spicy chili sauce...to enhance the beefy flavour.... the key is to let the 'gravy' form by stewing it until the juices thicken without any flour added; the cheaper cuts of beef are better for this, as they are more flavourful and provide more 'gravy'.( I use boneless short rib roast that I cube, so that I know the consistency will be uniform) if at the end the stew seems watery, then boil it down until you like the consistency, if it seems dry, then add some water.

I've been making this for years now, and the recipe really is great as-is. However, I believe it originally specified kosher salt and this may be why some are complaining about the saltiness. Kosher salt is less "salty" than table salt. Decrease by half to start, then add more to taste.

This is a very tasty recipe. After browning and mixing everything in the pan, I transferred it to a a crockpot and cooked it on high for 4 hours because I didn't want to have to keep an eye on the stove. I did substitute a can of beef broth for the water and, as Poch suggested, added 3 tblsp Worcestershire sauce, 2 tblsp brown sugar, 1 tblsp vinegar, 2 tblsp catsup. I also added about a cup of canned, diced tomatoes (drained) and small jar of sliced mushrooms (drained) because I am trying to add more veggies to my diet. I'm sure it is great without the additional ingredients, too.
I used ground turkey, chicken broth, extra paprika, zucchini, mushrooms, and cooked it for 10 minutes in the Instant Pot after sauteeing the turkey with an onion.

My four children - picky eaters - loved this meal. I had only rotini noodles so that's what I served with the goulash, and the kids loved it. I I didn't have beef broth so I followed suggestions of others and I added 3 tablespoons of Worcestershire sauce, 1 tablespoon brown sugar, 1 tablespoon of vinegar and a dash or two of hot sauce . I used 1/4 cup tomato paste plus I chopped up a fresh tomato and a green pepper and added them along with all the liquids. I cooked it on medium in the crock pot for 3 hours.
Simple & Delicious!!!! Only thing I did was add 2 TBSP of Worcestershire Sause & 1 TBSB Apple Cider Vinegar.

I love the recipe… been using now for at least 11 years if not longer. The only thing I do extra is season the onions with salt and pepper and I eyeball the salt for the dish as well as garlic because we love garlic I add a splash of Worcestershire in the dish and cook it for 2 hours also I substitute the water with beef broth. The kids love it we put it over egg noodles and voila…
Cooked with beef broth, modified with Worchestershire, ketchup, and brown sugar, and allowed to simmer for an extra half hour at low heat. It's delicious.

I love this base recipe! Some of the adding to the dish I did but there’s a couple of things I did that wasn’t stated in other reviews I read, I used a couple bay leafs and a can of Rotel. Also when browning meat afterwards I flour meat and add a little unsalted butter so meat doesn’t stick and it helps meat get a nice flour coating. My husband has been asking me for this dish ever since I started making. Thank You!

YUMMO! My husband really loved this recipe a lot! I followed the recipe with a few exceptions. I saw some reviews that said to use fresh tomato instead of tomato paste, and I used beef broth instead of water and once I was done browning my meat and unions I added the rest of the ingredients and cooked it in the oven in my Dutch oven on 325-350 for 2 hours! The meat was perfectly tender! Served over egg noodles and garnished with sour cream

Definitely a keeper and will use this recipe again! Super easy with ingredients I already have on hand.

My adjustments based on previous reviews (thank you BTY): Doubled the sweet paprika, added 4 cloves of garlic, used beef bouillon, chunks of carrots. I raided freezer and used Trader Joe's mushroom medley mix and sprinkled some gravy thickener last 15-20 min of cooking. Everything cooked in 2-hrs. Served with rice.
more minced garlic for more Hungarian flavor!.Yummy! less salt for sure! Dietary changes in my family!
I am Hungarian. Goulash is not made with any form of tomato. It's not even close to what Hungarian Goulash tastes like.

I was skeptical about it only calling for 3/4 cup water, but was proven wrong! It was very easy to prepare and I had all the ingredients on hand-no extra store runs. Cheap, easy and tasty. It’s a winner.
I made this dish and everyone raved about it. Yep, it’s a keeper. I substituted three things and used olive oil, regular paprika, and stew beef It came out great.
The very best original hungarian goulosh l have ever made!!!
Easy and delicious! I used 1/2 of Marsala Wine for 1/2 of water. Good! Noodles are good but my biscuits are better!
Added a splash of balsamic vinegar! Incredible flavor and easy to make!
